On Thu, 8 Apr 2010, Cesar Zucco wrote:

> Just realized that converting the clustering variable pty to a numeric
> vector (instead of a factor) solves the problem!
>
> Sorry for the trouble!
>
> Cesar
>
> -----Original Message-----
> From: Cesar Zucco [mailto:zucco-uX/v2g6dJhCyum0STUha2w at public.gmane.org]
> Sent: Wednesday, April 07, 2010 8:46 PM
> To: Kosuke Imai; sayan dasgupta
> Cc: zelig-boHuZhbfW+Y6DHxCPSz5rL5+avTOL6Rl at public.gmane.org; Terry Therneau; Terry Therneau
> Subject: Re: [zelig] Re: robust se's in zelig's tobit
>
> Dear Sayan,
>
> Here's a quick follow up to the cluster issue in Zelig that circulated a
> few
> days back. Sorry to keep you on this.
>
> I was able to run clustering with tobit in Zelig but I'm having some
> trouble
> with the post-estimation commands. If I ran this  without clustering,
> post
> estimation works fine:
>
> tob4 <-
> zelig(mrelideal~relideo+incab+prespty+legis,model="tobit",data=data.set)
> x.out <- setx(tob4,incab=0,legis=1995,relideo=mean(data.set$relideo))
> x.in <- setx(tob4,incab=1,legis=1995,relideo=mean(data.set$relideo))
> x.out
>  (Intercept)  relideo incab presptyTRUE legis1990 legis1995 legis2000
> 1           1 2.086757     0           0         0         1         0
> sims <- sim(tob4, x = x.out, x1 = x.in)
>
>
> However, if I ran this with the clustering, setx does not treat the
> clustering correctly.
>
> tob4 <-
> zelig(mrelideal~relideo+incab+prespty+legis,cluster="pty",robust=T,
> model="tobit",data=data.set)
> x.out <- setx(tob4,incab=0,legis=1995,relideo=mean(data.set$relideo))
> x.in <- setx(tob4,incab=1,legis=1995,relideo=mean(data.set$relideo))
> x.out
>  (Intercept)  relideo incab presptyTRUE legis1990 legis1995 legis2000
> cluster(pty)PC cluster(pty)PN cluster(pty)NE
> 1           1 2.086757     0           0         0         1         0
> 0              0              0
> sim(tob4, x = x.out, x1 = x.in)
>> Error in sim.coef %*% t(x) : non-conformable arguments
>
>
> I tried getting rid of the extra values in x.out by brute force (by
> deleting
> any columns with cluster in the name but I think sim is using the wrong
> variance-cov matrix to draw the simulations.
>
> Any workarounds?
>
> Thanks,
>
>
> Cesar Zucco
>
> On 3/19/10 8:54 AM, "Kosuke Imai" <kimai-cTYGs6MY1n4q5t9Oc1ygMg at public.gmane.org> wrote:
>
>> Great. Thanks, Sayan!
>>
>> Kosuke
>
>

messages.subject: Missing values in x
messages.body_plain:
Dear Colleagues,

 

I am running an "ls" model in Zelig, using the following code: 

 

z.out <-
zelig(primpac~lg_nrpar+I(lg_nrpar^2)+complem+ac+r_object+r_tracost+q_2+q_6+b
efore+senior+pr_eufp+thematic+instrument+lg_pr_duration+lg_pr_funding+q_16+q
_20+q_23a+q_23b+q_23c+q_23d+q_23e+q_23f+commun+coord+dynam+uni_vs_entr,
model = "ls",

robust = TRUE,data = Dataset)

 

Then I set the range of values of my variable of interest: 

size.range <- seq(from = 0.301, to  = 2.076, by = 0.10)

 

And then I set x.low and x.high as follows:

 

x.low <- setx(z.out, pr_eufp = 0, lg_nrpar = size.range)

 

x.high <- setx(z.out, pr_eufp = 1, lg_nrpar = size.range)

 

When I run 

s.out <- sim(z.out, x = x.low, x1 = x.high)

 

I get the following error message: 

 

ERROR: infinite or missing values in 'x'

 

Can please anyone explain the meaning of this message and what am I doing
wrong?

 

Many thanks in advance,

 

Yiannis

messages.subject: Re: Missing values in x
messages.body_plain:
zelig does not handle missing values.  You might want to try 
multiply-impute the missing data using the software such as Amelia and 
then use them in zelig.

Kosuke

-- 
Department of Politics
Princeton University
http://imai.princeton.edu

messages.subject: viewing data with predicted values and applying data to very large holdout sets for viewing
messages.subject_clean: viewing data with predicted values and applying data to very large holdout sets for viewing
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,

Can someone please point me to the section in the zelig manual where it 
tells me how to apply a model (such as the logit or weibull) and save a 
dataset into my c-drive with 2 new variables appended from the model at the 
end, one which has the prediction from the model appended and another 
variable that has the probability associated with the category it is 
predicted into.

For example (logit model)

> z.out <- zelig(vote ~gender, model = "logit", + data = turnout[1:20000,])

The saved file would enable me to compute by hand (observed  + expected) and 
examine the probability of predicted values etc  .....

I would like to open or view this model in a package like excel as a .csv 
file.

ID, gender, vote (bush or obama ), probability of voting obama
1, 33, male, obama, .73
2, 27, male, obama, .64

I also want to apply the following function, and to see how the model 
performs on a large scale set of holdout data.
> z.out <- zelig(vote ~ race + educate, model = "logit", + data = 
> turnout[1:20000,])
> x.out <- setx(z.out, data = turnout[2100:400000,])

how do I save and store this x.out (400,000) + cases for viewing in a 
package like spss or excel

Finally, how do I save the 's.out' (1000 simulations) files for examination 
later also

Thanks Paul

messages.body_plain:
I suggest that you start by reading Chapters 3-4 of the Zelig manual.

There really is no reason to export any data from R to Excel or SPSS,
particularly because it sounds like the calculations that you want to
perform can be done with built-in Zelig commands, or at most 1 line of
R code.
